samples.summary: The "mounted on every v1 controller" test is a hand-maintained enumeration, so it cannot fail for a NEW controller — contradicting the comment that claims it will
samples.evidence: The `describe('is mounted on every v1 controller')` block hardcodes six controller classes (lines 64-71). The comment at lines 58-62 asserts "this test fails if one does not [carry the guard]", but a seventh v1 controller added to `api-v1.module.ts` without the guard would simply not be in the list and the suite stays green — exactly the regression the guard was written to prevent. The list is derivable: `packages/backend/src/api/v1/api-v1.module.ts:28-35` already declares the authoritative `controllers` array, which `Reflect.getMetadata('controllers', ApiV1Module)` would expose. As written the test documents today's state rather than enforcing the invariant it claims.

samples.summary: The behavioral assertion that a read-scoped key stores nothing was deleted and replaced with a comment; no test covers the "nothing is stored" claim
samples.evidence: The removed test asserted both `rejects...ForbiddenException` and `expect(fileService.upload).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`. Its replacement is a prose comment (lines 59-62) that claims "Nothing is stored, because the guard runs ahead of the multipart handler" — an ordering property no test in the diff exercises. The new guard spec only calls `guard.canActivate()` directly and reads `__guards__` metadata; it never boots the Nest request pipeline. I searched `packages/backend/test/*.e2e-spec.ts` (including `api-key-http.e2e-spec.ts`) for `scopes` / `write access` and found no HTTP-level scope enforcement test, so nothing anywhere covers the guard actually running before the FileInterceptor.

samples.summary: Surviving tests named for scope behaviour are now vacuous with respect to scopes — the handler no longer reads `req.user.scopes`
samples.evidence: `it('allows a write-scoped API key')` (line 64) passes `req(true, ['read','write'])`, and `it('does not scope-check a JWT caller...')` (line 76) passes a JWT. With the `if (req.user.isApiKey && !req.user.scopes?.includes('write'))` check deleted from `files.controller.ts`, both tests would pass identically with `scopes: ['read']`, with `scopes: undefined`, or with the scope concept removed entirely. The same applies to `documents.controller.spec.ts:62` ('allows a write-scoped API key without a membership check') — it still meaningfully asserts the membership skip, but nothing about the scope in its name. These read as scope coverage while being incapable of failing on scope regressions.

samples.summary: The new shared codec has no direct unit test, and its write-side non-finite/unknown-alignment drop is untested in any suite
samples.evidence: `serializeBlockStyleAttrs` drops a numeric field when `!Number.isFinite(value)` and drops `alignment` when `!isBlockAlignment(...)`; `serializeMarginFromEdgeAttrs` does the same. Every new test I found exercises only the READ side of that contract: `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.spec.ts` ('reads a legacy poisoned block style...', 'reads a legacy poisoned header marginFromEdge...') hand-builds a poisoned Tree rather than going through the serializer, and the write-side tests only cover ABSENT fields (`style: {}`, header without `marginFromEdge`). The same is true of the frontend tests in `yorkie-doc-store.test.ts` ('block style codec' describe). No test writes `{ lineHeight: NaN }` or `{ alignment: 'middle' }` through `writeDocsRoot`/`setDocument` and asserts the attribute is omitted. There is also no `packages/docs/test/model/crdt-attrs.test.ts` at all, so `isBlockAlignment` / `BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS` — now a public export consumed by the backend validator — are only covered transitively.
searchedFor: grep 'crdt-attrs' in packages/docs (only src/index.ts and src/node.ts)

samples.summary: `markerToXml`'s changed drop-condition for bullet colour has no direct export test
samples.evidence: The condition changed from `marker.color != null` to `if (buClr)` where `buClr = storedColorToThemeColor(marker.color)`, so a marker colour that is not expressible as a hex triplet (e.g. `'red'`, `''`, `{kind:'srgb',value:''}`) now silently drops `<a:buClr>`. Grepping `buClr` across `packages/slides` returns only import-side tests (`test/import/pptx/text.test.ts:232,274`, `master.test.ts:72`) and fixtures; the only export-side coverage is the generic bullet-marker round-trip at `test/export/pptx/round-trip.test.ts:154`, which uses a valid colour and therefore cannot distinguish the old behaviour from the new. The unset/unexpressible cases the change introduces are untested, unlike the parallel run-colour changes which got explicit tests in `text.test.ts`.

samples.summary: Several new validator branches added by this diff have no test exercising them
samples.evidence: Tested: header/footer malformed blocks, non-finite `header.marginFromEdge`, table-cell missing `style`, malformed inlines. Untested branches I could not find any case for in `docs-content.controller.spec.ts`: `assertValidHeaderFooter`'s `'${path}' must be an object` (a non-object `header`) and `'${path}.blocks' must be an array`; `assertValidLayout`'s `Invalid layout at ${path}: not an object`; and, in the docs arm's inline walk, the `'style' must be an object` branch (only the `'text' must be a string` branch is covered by 'rejects a malformed inline'). Each is a distinct 400 message this change introduces.
searchedFor: reviewed all new spec cases in the diff for header/footer/layout non-object payloads

samples.summary: The new `putContent` wrapper adds no test value while its comment implies guard coverage the spec does not have
samples.evidence: `const putContent = (workspaceId, documentId, body) => controller.putContent(workspaceId, documentId, body)` is a pure pass-through; the comment above it (lines 65-68) explains guard enforcement, but the alias neither exercises nor asserts anything about `ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard`. It is also applied inconsistently — the chart-repair test at line 1553 still calls `controller.putContent` directly — so the indirection buys nothing but a diff-wide rename.
